title: Quick ADHD Test
summary: Ten personal questions about attention, organisation, restlessness and impulsivity.

landing.intro: Do unfinished tasks, lost time or constant distraction feel far too familiar? These 10 quick questions look at patterns adults often miss.

about.body:
This ten-question self-check asks about attention, organisation, time management, forgetfulness, restlessness and impulsivity. It groups your answers into a descriptive pattern summary; it does not calculate whether you have ADHD.

ADHD is a developmental condition, so a professional assessment considers whether traits began in childhood, persist over time, appear in more than one setting and interfere with daily life. Stress, sleep problems, anxiety, depression and physical conditions can cause similar experiences.

steps: Choose the answer that best reflects your usual experience.
Think across home, work, study and relationships where relevant.
Reveal your personal attention summary after all ten questions.

about.disclaimer: For general information only. This is not a diagnostic test, validated ADHD screener or substitute for a professional assessment. It cannot confirm or rule out ADHD or another condition. If attention, restlessness or impulsivity causes persistent difficulty, speak with a qualified healthcare professional.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Your ten answers have been reviewed and your personal attention summary is ready to reveal.

profile-1.title: No Single Pattern Dominated
profile-1.copy: Your answers did not highlight one dominant attention or impulsivity pattern. That cannot rule out ADHD, especially when people use strong coping strategies. Seek professional advice if persistent difficulties remain concerning.

profile-2.title: Executive Tasks May Be Taking Extra Effort
profile-2.copy: Your answers centred on focus, organisation, time, remembering or completing tasks. These difficulties can have several explanations. If they are persistent across settings, a qualified professional can help assess the wider picture.

profile-3.title: Your Internal Pace May Be Running Fast
profile-3.copy: Your answers highlighted restlessness, interrupting, impatience or acting before thinking. A longstanding pattern across more than one setting is worth discussing with a qualified professional, particularly when it affects daily life.

profile-4.title: The Full Pattern Is Worth Exploring
profile-4.copy: Your answers suggest that attention, restlessness or impulsivity may be longstanding and disruptive across important areas of life. This result is not a diagnosis, but it may be a useful prompt to ask about a professional ADHD assessment.

adhd-q1.question: How often do you begin an important task but struggle to finish the final details?

answers.a4: Very often, and deadlines or responsibilities suffer

adhd-q2.question: How easily do unrelated thoughts, sounds or notifications pull your attention away?

answers.a3: Often, even when I want to focus

adhd-q3.question: What is planning and organising a multi-step task like for you?

answers.a3: I rush or jump between steps before finishing
answers.a4: It regularly prevents me completing important tasks

adhd-q4.question: How often do appointments, everyday tasks or important items slip your mind?

adhd-q5.question: How do you feel when you need to remain seated or quiet for a long time?

answers.a3: I fidget or feel driven to move
answers.a4: The restlessness is intense and difficult to manage

adhd-q6.question: How often do you interrupt, finish another person's sentence or struggle to wait?

answers.a3: Often before I can stop myself
answers.a4: Very often, and it affects conversations or relationships

adhd-q7.question: How often do you make quick decisions before considering the consequences?

answers.a3: Often in conversation, spending or plans

adhd-q8.question: When several tasks compete for attention, what usually happens?

answers.a1: I prioritise and work through them
answers.a3: I jump between them because staying still feels difficult
answers.a4: I become stuck or leave important tasks unfinished

adhd-q9.question: Looking back, when did similar patterns first become noticeable?

answers.a2: Some attention difficulties were present in childhood
answers.a3: Restlessness or impulsivity was present in childhood
answers.a4: Several patterns began before age 12 and continued

adhd-q10.question: How widely do these patterns affect your life?

answers.a2: Mostly attention or organisation in one setting
answers.a3: Mostly restlessness or impulsivity in one setting
answers.a4: They persist in two or more settings and interfere with daily life
